BundleExportConfig.description:
There will be one file per sensor id and atmospheric profile and retrieval algorithm combination.

The final name looks like `em27-retrieval-bundle-$SENSOR_ID-$RETRIEVAL_ALGORITHM-$ATMOSPHERIC_PROFILE-$FROM_DATE-$TO_DATE$BUNDLE_SUFFIX.$OUTPUT_FORMAT`, e.g.`em27-retrieval-bundle-ma-GGG2020-proffast-2.4-20150801-20240523-v2.1.csv`. The bundle suffix is optional and can be used to distinguish between different internal datasets.

GroundPressure.description:
Format of the ground pressure files. We support any text file that stores one data point per row and separates the columns with a comma, space, or tab, i.e. CSV, TSV, or space-separated files. Using the `file_regex` field, you specify which files to consider for a given sensor id and date.

You have to specify the columns that contain the date and time of the data. There is three options to specify this - the CLI will complain if you configure none or more than one of these options:

* One column with a datetime string -> configure `datetime_column` and `datetime_column_format`
* Two columns, one with the date and one with the time -> configure `date_column`, `date_column_format`, `time_column`, and `time_column_format`
* One column with a unix timestamp -> configure `unix_timestamp_column` and `unix_timestamp_column_format`

path.description: Directory path to ground pressure files. You should use absolute paths, but if you need relative paths, then this is relative to the caller of the CLI or the pipeline's entrypoint.

file_regex.description: A regex string to match the ground pressure file names. In this string, you can use the placeholders `$(SENSOR_ID)`, `$(YYYY)`, `$(YY)`, `$(MM)`, and `$(DD)` to make this regex target a certain station and date. The placeholder `$(DATE)` is a shortcut for `$(YYYY)$(MM)$(DD)`.
file_regex.title: File Regex

separator.description: Separator used in the ground pressure files. Only needed and used if the file format is `text`.
separator.title: Separator

datetime_column.description: Column name in the ground pressure files that contains the datetime.
datetime_column.title: Datetime Column

datetime_column_format.description: Format of the datetime column in the ground pressure files.
datetime_column_format.title: Datetime Column Format

date_column.description: Column name in the ground pressure files that contains the date.
date_column.title: Date Column

date_column_format.description: Format of the date column in the ground pressure files.
date_column_format.title: Date Column Format

time_column.description: Column name in the ground pressure files that contains the time.
time_column.title: Time Column

time_column_format.description: Format of the time column in the ground pressure files.
time_column_format.title: Time Column Format

unix_timestamp_column.description: Column name in the ground pressure files that contains the unix timestamp.
unix_timestamp_column.title: Unix Timestamp Column

unix_timestamp_column_format.description: Format of the unix timestamp column in the ground pressure files. I.e. is the Unix timestamp in seconds, milliseconds, etc.?
unix_timestamp_column_format.title: Unix Timestamp Column Format

pressure_column.description: Column name in the ground pressure files that contains the pressure.
pressure_column.title: Pressure Column

pressure_column_format.description: Unit of the pressure column in the ground pressure files.
pressure_column_format.title: Pressure Column Format

GroundPressure.title: GroundPressure

If used, the pipeline computes the solar noon time using `skyfield` and averages the local pressure over the time period noon-2h to noon+2h.

use_ifg_corruption_filter.description: Whether to use the ifg corruption filter. If activated, we will only pass the interferograms to the retrieval algorithm that pass the filter - i.e. that won't cause it to crash.

pressure_calibration_offsets.description: Maps sensor IDS to pressure calibration offsets. If not set, it is set to 0 for each sensor. `corrected_pressure = input_pressure * calibration_factor + calibration_offset`

StrictDirectoryPath.description:
A pydantic model that validates a directory path.

Example usage:

```python
class MyModel(pyndatic.BaseModel):
    path: StrictDirectoryPath

m = MyModel(path='/path/to/directory') # validates that the directory exists
```

The validation can be ignored by setting the context variable:

```python
m = MyModel.model_validate(
    {"path": "somenonexistingpath"},
    context={"ignore-path-existence": True},
) # does not raise an error
```
StrictDirectoryPath.title: StrictDirectoryPath
